en: Buddhavamsa 3.
The Lineage of Dīpaṅkara Buddha:
"Then, having fed them..."
They went for refuge to that Teacher Dīpaṅkara, together with his Saṅgha, the Leader of the World.
The Tathāgata established some in the going for refuge,
and some in the five precepts.
In the tenfold morality,
he bestows supreme asceticism upon anyone who gives it,
along with the four most excellent fruits.
To some he gives the incomparable states;
to some, the analytical knowledges;
to some, the sublime attainments.
The Bull among Men bestows eight [attainments];
he grants three types of clear knowledge to some,
and the six higher knowledges to others.
With that method, the Great Sage exhorted the multitude of people;
by that means, it became widespread.
The teaching of the Lord of the World.
He who was named Dīpaṅkara had broad jaws and shoulders like those of a bull.
He delivers many people and liberates them from an evil destiny;
seeing those who are capable of being awakened, he brings them to enlightenment.
Even from a hundred thousand yojanas away,
having arrived in an instant,
the Great Sage awakens him.
At the first realization, the Buddha awakened one hundred koṭis;
at the second realization, the Protector—
He awakened ninety million beings.
And when the Buddha taught the Dhamma within the celestial abode,
There was a third realization for ninety thousand koṭis;
there were three such assemblies.
Of the Teacher Dīpaṅkara,
there was a first assembly of one hundred thousand times ten million.
Again, when the Conqueror had gone to seclusion at Nāradakūṭa,
the taints were exhausted and the stains were removed.
Hundreds of millions gathered together at that time when the Great Hero was upon the Sudassana mountain of stone.
The Great Sage offered hospitality to nine thousand million [monks],
and to twenty thousand [others].
There was a realization of the Dhamma;
from the number of those who realized it, one or two,
they were incalculable.
At that time, the realm of the Blessed One Dīpaṅkara was widespread, well-known, prosperous, and flourishing.
The Dispensation was thoroughly purified.
Four hundred thousand [monks],
possessing the six direct knowledges and great psychic power, [were there].
They always attend upon Dīpaṅkara, the Knower of the World;
whoever they may be at that time, [they all do so].
They abandon human existence;
those trainees who have not yet attained their goal are subject to reproach.
The well-flowered word of the Teaching,
by the Tathāgatas, the Arahants,
those whose taints are destroyed and who are stainless.
It always shines beautifully.
There was a city named Rammavatī,
and a kshatriya king named Sudeva.
The mother of the Teacher Dīpaṅkara was named Sumedhā;
for ten thousand years—
He lived in a house;
there were three supreme palaces: for swans, curlews, and peacocks.
Three hundred thousand women were beautifully adorned;
that woman named Padumā—
Usabhakkhandha was his biological son.
Having seen four omens,
he departed by means of an elephant vehicle.
For ten full months the Conqueror applied himself to striving;
having practiced the course of striving, he—
The Sage awoke to the mind;
being entreated by Brahmā,
the Great Sage Dīpaṅkara consented.
The Great Hero set the wheel in motion at Nandārāma in the Śrīgṛha,
sitting at the foot of the Śirīṣa tree.
[He was] Akā, the crusher of the non-Buddhist sectarians.
Sumaṅgala and Tissa were his two chief disciples.
Sāgata was the attendant of the Teacher Dīpaṅkara;
and there were also Nandā and Sunandā.
were his chief female disciples;
the Bodhi tree of that Blessed One is called the Pipphali.
There were two chief attendants named Tapussa and Bhallika; there was also a female attendant named Koṇā,
who was possessed of beauty.
Of the Teacher Dīpaṅkara.
The Great Sage Dīpaṅkara was eighty cubits in height.
He shines like a lamp-tree,
like a king of sal trees in full bloom.
For a hundred thousand years,
Such was the lifespan of that Great Sage;
remaining for that long,
he delivered many people across.
Having kindled the True Dhamma and having brought many people across,
like a blazing mass of fire, he has gone out.
He has attained Nibbāna along with his disciples.
Such is his supernormal power and such is his glory,
including those precious wheel-treasures upon his feet.
All that has vanished;
are not all conditioned things empty?
Dīpaṅkara was the Victor, the Teacher.
He attained final nibbāna at Nandārāma;
right there stands his Jina-stūpa,
thirty-six yojanas in height.
The first lineage is that of the Blessed One Dīpaṅkara.
